Dish Your Way

How we would make it, and have the first episode out by 31 October.

This answers what you asked us on 9 October: how we'd approach the format, what it costs, how the three weeks run, who the cooks could be, and the work that shows we understand food. It is written so it can be forwarded as it is.

The whole thing on one page.

What

Dish Your Way, your format as you drew it: one dish, two home cooks from two states, Kunal Kapur tastes blind and picks a bowl. The pilot is khichdi, Gujarat against Bengal. Each episode gives a 60-second reel, a 6 to 8 minute episode, two 15-second teasers and stills for the grid.

When

Your yes by Wednesday 14 October. Shoot on Wednesday 21 October, Kunal's block after lunch. First cut on Monday 26. The pilot reel goes out on Friday 30 October, the episode on YouTube behind it, reels two and three the following week.

How much

Inside ₹13 lakh. Three episodes from one shoot day: ₹12,90,000. The pilot alone: ₹8,00,000. Kunal's fee, GST and paid media sit outside these. Every line is on page 15, and every line is a placeholder until we fix the scope together.

Who

Harsh Arya leads and is your one call. With him: the producer who ran the Borges films, a director and DOP who shoot food, a food stylist, an editor. Kunal's block is two to three hours on the shoot day.

From you

Five things by Wednesday: the dish list, Kunal's date, a founder's date, the packs we shoot with, and one person who approves names, scripts and cuts within four hours. Page 16 has the list.

Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight01 · The brief

What we heard on 9 October.

Your brief, in your words, so you can check we have it right before anyone else reads this.

The format

One heritage dish an episode. Two home cooks, two states, the same dish, a different preparation. Built for reels and for long form. Kunal Kapur tastes blind and judges.

The point of view

Everyone in the category talks about transparency, traceability and purity. You want to show food at its truest expression, with the product as the catalyst and not the subject.

The look

Fresh, and not done before. An open set with greenery that looks like Anveshan. A split screen, so both kitchens are always in view.

The people

Kunal judges. One or two of the founders on camera with him, so their faces become familiar and, in time, the brand's own.

The cooks

Found the organic way where possible: a contest on your own creator base, with a shoot with Kunal and a page in a recipe book as the prize.

The money

Around ₹13 lakh for production, editing and sourcing the cooks. Kunal is handled by you. A placeholder costing is fine for now: studio or outdoor, cameras, two or three stations, half a day.

The clock

Out by the end of October, before the festive weeks. As few meetings as possible, on both sides.

The partnership

You keep few partners and want one who can do many things and grow with you. If this works, there is more to do together.

Tell us what we got wrong and the deck changes the same day. We read this as one team: you and we both have to take it to the founders.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight02 · Our inputs

Five things we would add. The format stays yours.

Each one is small and practical, and none of them changes the six beats in your storyboard.

The Anveshan beat is the same three seconds in every episode.

Ghee hits the pan, or the dough is rolled, in the same place in the edit with the same sound every time. Your idea of the product as the catalyst becomes something people wait for, and it never has to be sold.

One jar, two kitchens.

Your two-tablespoon rule becomes the house rule of the show: the same measure from the same jar, each cook's own recipe. It is the fairest thing in the show, and it is the product.

Cast pairs who already know each other.

A couple, two sisters, two flatmates from two states. The teasing is real, so the comments carry on after the reel ends. That is what a real pair's audience does, and it is why we would start the casting there.

Pick pairs that look different on a split screen.

Two yellow khichdis read as one dish. Gujarat's bowl is pale and soft, with the ghee poured on at the table; Bengal's bhoger khichuri is golden, with the moong roasted first and the potato and cauliflower fried in ghee. Your own line, "ghee abhi ya end mein?", is the difference between the two states.

Shoot three in a day. The shortlist casts them; the contest casts the next three.

One set-up, two stations, three dishes: three reels and three episodes for one day of crew. The pilot never waits for a ten-day contest, and the contest winners get the November batch, with Kunal.

One more, for Kunal's team: he fronted Saffola's regional cook-off this April, city against city with large creators. Dish Your Way is home cooks, one jar and a blind taste. Worth saying out loud, so the difference is clear to his team and to the audience.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight03 · The pilot

Khichdi, Gujarat against Bengal, as we would shoot it.

Your six beats, with what the camera does in each. The cooks cook in real time; the sixty seconds are cut from about forty minutes.

0–4s · The face-off

Both cooks at their stations, the VS card over a two-shot, the host's line.

Camera

A locked wide on both stations, with a slow push in.

The food

Two pots, still empty. The jar between them.

4–12s · The argument

A split screen of the two kitchens, one family line each to camera, hands already working.

Camera

An overhead above each station for the split; a camera on each face.

The food

Gujarat washes rice and moong together. Bengal dry-roasts the sona moong first. The difference starts here.

12–18s · The rule

Two measured spoons from one jar. "Bas do chamach ghee."

Camera

The macro lens on the spoon and the ghee going in. This is the Anveshan beat: three seconds, sound up.

The food

The ghee blooms. Bengal fries potato and cauliflower in it; Gujarat holds its spoon back.

18–36s · The cook

Matched actions cut against each other, the clock in the corner, one rival glance.

Camera

The overheads on the pans; a third camera roams for hands and faces.

The food

Gujarat's pot goes soft and pale with turmeric. Bengal's takes bay leaf, ginger, cumin, a pinch of sugar and the fried vegetables, and turns golden.

36–52s · The blind taste

Kunal in the eye mask, two plain bowls marked A and B, the spoon, the pause. The cooks wait.

Camera

The judge camera on Kunal, the overheads on the bowls, the cooks' faces on the reverse.

The food

Served the same way in the same bowls. No garnish that gives a state away.

52–60s · The reveal

The vote is locked, the mask comes off, one reason, both cooks in frame. "Tumhari khichdi kaisi?"

Camera

Back to the wide, then down to the dish.

The food

The two bowls side by side for the last frame, each with its state's name.

The six frames are direction frames, generated to set the look; nothing has been shot yet. Sound: lavaliers on both cooks and the host, a boom on the pans. Light: soft daylight or a daylight rig, so the ghee reads gold and not orange. Styling: a kansa thali for Gujarat, a plain white bowl for Bengal, brass and steel on the stations, and the pack by the stove, never in the centre.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight04 · The set

Three places we could shoot it. We would pick the farmhouse.

You asked whether it is a studio or outdoors. Here are the three ways it can go, with what each costs and what each looks like.

A kitchen studio in Delhi NCR

Rentable by the day, two stations possible, power, water and light under our control, bookable in a day. It looks like a studio unless we dress it, so we bring in the greens, the cane, the brass and the raw cotton.

₹30,000 to ₹60,000 a day.

Best for certainty on the dates.

A restaurant in its off hours

A real kitchen with real heat, such as a farm-to-table restaurant at an Aerocity hotel. Only before noon or after service, light we do not control, and usually against a credit rather than rent.

₹0 to ₹50,000, depending on the arrangement.

Best for the look of a working kitchen, if their hours fit ours.

A farmhouse with an open kitchen

Chhatarpur or Gurugram, a garden behind the stations, daylight through the day: the open green set you described. It needs a generator and a food-safe kitchen check at the recce, and we have shot in houses like these before.

₹40,000 to ₹80,000 a day.

Our pick for looking like Anveshan, if the recce is done by Monday 19.

Whichever we choose, both stations are built the same, down to the pan, the spoon and the jar. The set is dressed once and holds for all three episodes.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight05 · The cooks

Where the two cooks in every episode come from.

Our shortlist

Home-cook creators with real roots in one state, 20K to 500K followers, recipe-first feeds. The Borges filter: people who cook on camera, not people who review restaurants. The next page has fifteen of them.

Your creator base, through the contest

An open call on your handles for ten days. We shortlist ten, speak to four on video, and cast two an episode. Page 9 has the mechanic. The winners cook in the November batch.

A real home cook, paired with a creator

A grandmother or an aunt beside a creator from the other state. The most believable pair on the show, and the one that needs a day of handling, which we do.

What we look for

Hands that know the dish. A face that can be teased. One family line about the recipe that is true. Hindi or Hinglish on camera.

Every pair

  • One cook from each state. A prior relationship where we can find one.
  • Signed on a one-page agreement: the appearance, the use of the footage on your channels and in your ads, the product in frame.
  • Local cooks first. Anyone outside Delhi adds ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 in travel and a night's stay.
  • Briefed on the rule, not on the recipe. Their recipe is theirs.
  • Fees at cost, confirmed to you before we book.
The contest and the shortlist run side by side: the shortlist casts the first three episodes in the week of 13 October, the contest casts the next three.

Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight06 · The contest

Cook with Kunal: a ten-day open call on your own base.

Your idea, laid out as a run of days. It uses the creator base you already pay for, and it hands the winners to the November batch.

Day 1 · Wed 15 Oct

The post goes up on your handles, and a message goes to your creator base: "Your state's dish, in thirty seconds, with the jar in frame. Tag us." We write the post and the rules; you post them.

Days 1–7

Entries come in as reels on the show's hashtag. We watch every one and keep a running sheet: state, dish, hands, face, the story.

Day 8 · Thu 22 Oct

We send you a shortlist of ten with a line on each. You strike anyone you don't want.

Day 9

Four video calls. We check that the hands know the dish, that the face can be teased, and that the family line is true.

Day 10 · Sat 24 Oct

Two winners an episode, told the same day. Everyone shortlisted gets a hamper. The winners are cast for the November shoot, with Kunal.

The prize

A day cooking on the show with Kunal Kapur. A page in the recipe book with him, if you go ahead with the book. The episode on your handles, with their handle on it.

Who does what

We write the post and the rules, run the moderation and the calls, and do the agreements. You post it, and you pick from our ten. Terms, age and rights lines come from us, and your legal team sees them before the post goes up.

The contest runs 15 to 24 October, so its winners cannot be in the pilot. The pilot is cast from the shortlist, which is why the dates on page 14 hold.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight07 · On camera

What Kunal, the host and the founders each do.

Kunal, the judge

His block is two to three hours on the shoot day: the blind taste for every episode shot that day, the reveal with the cooks, and ten minutes of lines to camera, including three alternative opening hooks. If his date moves, his block becomes a separate half day and the cooks come back for the reveal. The blindfold means he never needs to see them cook.

The host

Your storyboard opens with a host line, and nobody has said yet who that is. Kunal can host and judge, which takes the most of his time; a founder can host the opening and the rule, which builds a founder's face, as you asked; or a voice and a card, which is fastest. We would put a founder on the opening and the rule, and keep Kunal for the verdict.

The founders

A recurring job, not a cameo: they bring the jar and say the rule, and they sit beside Kunal for the reveal. In the long episode, one moment of their own: what their mother made of the same dish. We coach on the day; the first episode tells us who is comfortable.

Later, once the faces are familiar: a plan for the founders as the brand's own creators, which we would bring to you after the first batch, not before.
Dish Your Way · × Ninety-EightProof 1 · The face-off

A face-off we made last month: Don Picante against Don Paloma.

For Servd on the Rocks, Swiggy's cocktail IP, with Don Julio: the Delhi edition, September 2026. Two cocktails, a table of guests, a running score and a winner. The closest thing to Dish Your Way we have made.

What we did

We ran the Delhi edition for Servd: the night at Chica, the two cocktails, the vote and this film.

What it shares with yours

Two versions of one thing, a maker behind each, a pick, a scoreboard and a winner, with the product in the making rather than in a sales break.

What it taught us

Name the two sides in the first five seconds and let the table argue. The vote is the content; the drink is the excuse.

Frames from the 39-second reel. We can send you the full film.

Dish Your Way · × Ninety-EightProof 3 · The book

We have shot food, launched restaurants, and worked around Kunal before.

Production

We ran the production for a MasterChef shoot at Thalassa in Goa: a set on the beach, a jib, three broadcast cameras, a band on the stage.

The F&B book behind it: One8 Commune, Slay Coffee, Yum Yum Cha, Farzi Cafe, Punjab Grill, Daryaganj, Hard Rock Cafe, and MEA with Chef Puneet of MasterChef Australia.

Kunal's world

We did the launch for Pincode, Kunal Kapur's restaurant, and we work with his partners there, who also run One8 Commune. We know how his team likes to work, and what they ask of a production.

For this show that means one thing in practice: his block is planned to the minute, and the food is ready before he walks in.

People, and formats that last

We build people as well as brands. Dr Prasanna Tantri of the ISB went from a faculty page to Know Time, The Prakhar Gupta Xperience and Vaad in a year of our work. Ishant Sharma is our exclusive talent, and fronted RuPay's first IPL campaign.

A show with a judge and two founders on camera is the same work: faces people come back for.

Dish Your Way · × Ninety-Eight08 · The three weeks

From your yes to the first reel: nineteen days.

Mon 12 Oct
You read this. A ten-minute call with the founders, if it helps.
Wed 14 Oct
Your yes. The dish list, Kunal's date and a founder's date are fixed. We book the location the same day.
Thu 15 – Sat 17
Casting calls and agreements. Recipes tested with the food stylist. The set drawn. The contest goes live on your handles.
Mon 19 Oct
Recce and tech check. Props and packs delivered. The run of show goes to you.
Tue 20 Oct
Dussehra. No shoot.
Wed 21 Oct
Shoot day. The cooks' block in the morning, Kunal's block after lunch. If his date moves: his block on Thu 22 or Sat 24, and the cooks come back for the reveal.
Thu 22 – Tue 27
The edit. First cut of the pilot reel on Mon 26, the episode on Tue 27.
Wed 28 Oct
Your notes, one round.
Thu 29 Oct
Final files, captions, cover frames and the teasers.
Fri 30 Oct
The pilot reel goes out. The episode follows on YouTube. Reels two and three go out the following week, before Diwali.

What keeps these dates

  • One person on your side who approves names, scripts and cuts within four hours, Monday to Saturday.
  • The three dishes locked by Wednesday 14.
  • Kunal's date in writing from his team.
  • A WhatsApp group with the three of us, and a line from us every evening on what moved.
  • One round of notes on each cut.
Diwali is Sunday 8 November. If the yes comes on Friday 16 instead of Wednesday 14, the shoot moves to Saturday 24 and the first reel to Tuesday 3 November, still ahead of it.
